recipes.name: Banana
steps: Peel and eat. Ripe means yellow with a few brown spots; green ones are firmer and less sweet.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 medium banana, about 7 to 8 inches long (about 4 oz of fruit without the peel). Buy a bunch of 5 to 6; they keep about 5 days on the counter.

recipes.name: Apple
steps: Wash and eat, or slice into wedges.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 medium apple, about the size of a baseball (3 inches across, about 6 oz). Keeps 3 to 4 weeks in the fridge.

recipes.name: Orange
steps: Peel, split into segments and eat.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 medium orange, about the size of a tennis ball (about 4.5 oz).

recipes.name: Pear
steps: Wash and eat. It is ripe when the neck gives a little under your thumb.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 medium pear (about 6 oz).

recipes.name: Grapes
steps: Rinse and eat. Keep them in the fridge.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 cup, about 30 grapes (about 5.3 oz).

recipes.name: Berries
steps: Rinse just before eating. Fresh or frozen both work.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 cup (about 5 oz). A pint container holds about 2 cups.

recipes.name: Pineapple Chunks
steps: Eat fresh or canned in juice (drain it).
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 cup of chunks (about 6 oz).

recipes.name: Half an Avocado
steps: Cut around the pit, twist apart and scoop out with a spoon. Add salt and lime if you like.
Keep the other half with the pit in, wrapped, in the fridge.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = half a medium avocado (about 2.5 oz of flesh). A ripe one gives slightly when squeezed.

recipes.name: Carrot Sticks
steps: Peel, cut into sticks and eat plain or with hummus.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 medium carrot (about 6 inches, 2 oz) or about 8 baby carrots.

recipes.name: Peanut Butter (2 Tbsp)
steps: Measure with a real tablespoon and level it off. Eat off the spoon, or spread on toast, apple or banana.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 2 tablespoons (32 g), about the size of a ping-pong ball. A 16 oz jar holds about 14 servings; a 28 oz jar about 25.

recipes.name: Almonds (1 oz)
steps: Count out about 23 almonds, or one small handful.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 oz, about 23 almonds (about 1/4 cup). Calorie-dense: a handful is fine, a full bag is not.

recipes.name: Peanuts (1 oz)
steps: One small handful, about 28 peanuts.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 oz (about 1/4 cup).

recipes.name: Plain Greek Yogurt
steps: Scoop into a bowl. Add berries, honey or oats if you want.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 3/4 cup, about one 6 oz single-serve cup (170 g). A 32 oz tub is about 5 servings. Pick nonfat or 2% plain; flavored cups add a lot of sugar.

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese
steps: Scoop into a bowl. Good with pineapple, berries or black pepper.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1/2 cup (about 4 oz). A 16 oz tub is about 4 servings.

recipes.name: Cheese (1 oz)
steps: Eat one string cheese stick, or a chunk about the size of two dice.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 oz, which is one string cheese stick or 1 slice of deli cheese.

recipes.name: Two Hard-Boiled Eggs
steps: Put eggs in a pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch and bring to a boil.
Turn off the heat, cover and let sit 11 minutes.
Move to ice water for 5 minutes, then peel.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 2 large eggs. Unpeeled hard-boiled eggs keep 7 days in the fridge. Make 6 to 12 at once.

recipes.name: Glass of Milk
steps: Pour 1 cup (8 fl oz).
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 cup. A gallon is 16 cups and a half-gallon is 8.

recipes.name: Slice of Toast
steps: Toast to golden brown.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 slice of sandwich bread (about 1 oz). Whole wheat has more fiber.

recipes.name: Air-Popped Popcorn
steps: Pop plain kernels in an air popper or a covered pot with a little oil, then salt lightly.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 3 cups popped (about 1 tbsp of kernels before popping).

recipes.name: Dark Chocolate (1 oz)
steps: Three or four small squares of a 70 to 85% bar.
recipes.notes: 1 serving = 1 oz (28 g).
